1 Then Jerubbaal, who is Gideon, and all the people who were with him, rose up early and encamped beside the spring of Harod. Midian’s camp was on the north side of them, by the hill of Moreh, in the valley.123✦ 2 Yahweh said to Gideon, “The people who are with you are too many for me to give the Midianites into their hand, lest Israel brag against me, saying, ‘My own hand has saved me.’45 3 Now therefore proclaim in the ears of the people, saying, ‘Whoever is fearful and trembling, let him return and depart from Mount Gilead.’” So twenty-two thousand of the people returned, and ten thousand remained.6✦ 4 Yahweh said to Gideon, “There are still too many people. Bring them down to the water7, and I will test them for you there. It shall be, that those whom I tell you, ‘This shall go with you,’ shall go with you; and whoever I tell you, ‘This shall not go with you,’ shall not go.”89 5 So he brought down the people to the water10; and Yahweh said to Gideon, “Everyone who laps of the water with his tongue, like a dog laps, you shall set him by himself; likewise everyone who bows down on his knees to drink.”1112✦ 6 The number of those who lapped, putting their hand to their mouth, was three hundred men; but all the rest of the people bowed down on their knees to drink water13.14✦ 7 Yahweh said to Gideon, “I will save you by the three hundred men who lapped15, and deliver the Midianites into your hand. Let all the other people go, each to his own place.”16171819✦ 8 So the people took food in their hand, and their trumpets; and he sent all the rest of the men of Israel to their own tents, but retained the three hundred men; and the camp of Midian was beneath him in the valley.2021✦ 9 That same night, Yahweh said to him, “Arise, go down into the camp, for I have delivered it into your hand.2223 10 But if you are afraid to go down, go with Purah your servant down to the camp.2425 11 You will hear what they say; and afterward your hands will be strengthened to go down into the camp.” Then went he down with Purah his servant to the outermost part of the armed men who were in the camp.26 12 The Midianites and the Amalekites and all the children of the east lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number, as the sand which is on the seashore for multitude.27✦ 13 When Gideon had come, behold, there was a man28 telling a dream to his fellow. He said, “Behold, I dreamed a dream; and behold, a cake of barley bread tumbled into the camp of Midian, came to the tent, and struck it so that it fell, and turned it upside down, so that the tent lay flat.”29✦ 14 His fellow answered, “This is nothing other than the sword of Gideon the son of Joash, a man30 of Israel. God31 has delivered Midian into his hand, with all the army.”32✦ 15 It was so, when Gideon heard the telling of the dream and its interpretation, that he worshiped. Then he returned into the camp of Israel and said, “Arise, for Yahweh has delivered the army of Midian into your hand!”3334✦ 16 He divided the three hundred men into three companies, and he put into the hands of all of them trumpets and empty35 pitchers, with torches within the pitchers.3637✦ 17 He said to them, “Watch me, and do likewise. Behold, when I come to the outermost part of the camp, it shall be that, as I do, so you shall do.38✦ 18 When I blow the trumpet, I and all who are with me, then blow the trumpets also on every side of all the camp, and shout, ‘For Yahweh and for Gideon!’”3940✦ 19 So Gideon and the hundred men who were with him came to the outermost part of the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, when they had but newly set the watch. Then they blew the trumpets and broke in pieces the pitchers that were in their hands.41✦ 20 The three companies blew the trumpets, broke the pitchers, and held the torches42 in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands with which to blow; and they shouted, “The sword of Yahweh and of Gideon!”434445✦ 21 They each stood in his place around the camp, and all the army ran; and they shouted, and put them to flight.4647✦ 22 They blew the three hundred trumpets, and Yahweh set every man48’s sword against his fellow and against all the army; and the army fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, as far as the border of Abel Meholah, by Tabbath.49505152✦ 23 The men of Israel were gathered together out of Naphtali, out of Asher, and out of all Manasseh, and pursued Midian.53✦ 24 Gideon sent messengers throughout all the hill country of Ephraim, saying, “Come down against Midian and take the waters54 before them as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan!” So all the men of Ephraim were gathered together and took the waters as far as Beth Barah, even the Jordan.5556✦ 25 They took the two princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at Oreb’s rock, and Zeeb they killed at Zeeb’s wine press, as they pursued Midian. Then they brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon beyond the Jordan.

8

123✦1 The men of Ephraim said to him, “Why have you treated us this way, that you didn’t call us when you went to fight with Midian?” They rebuked him sharply.4✦ 2 He said to them, “What have I now done in comparison with you? Isn’t the gleaning of the grapes of Ephraim better than the vintage of Abiezer?5✦ 3 God6 has delivered into your hand the princes of Midian, Oreb and Zeeb! What was I able to do in comparison with you?” Then their anger was abated toward him when he had said that.7✦ 4 Gideon came to the Jordan and passed over, he and the three hundred men who were with him, faint, yet pursuing.8 5 He said to the men of Succoth, “Please give loaves of bread to the people who follow me; for they are faint, and I am pursuing after Zebah and Zalmunna, the kings of Midian.”910✦ 6 The princes of Succoth said, “Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your army?”11 7 Gideon said, “Therefore when Yahweh has delivered Zebah and Zalmunna into my hand, then I will tear your flesh with the thorns of the wilderness and with briers.”1213 8 He went up there to Penuel, and spoke to them in the same way; and the men of Penuel answered him as the men of Succoth had answered.14✦ 9 He spoke also to the men of Penuel, saying, “When I come again in peace15, I will break down this tower.”16 10 Now Zebah and Zalmunna were in Karkor, and their armies with them, about fifteen thousand men, all who were left of all the army of the children of the east; for there fell one hundred twenty thousand men who drew sword.1718✦ 11 Gideon went up by the way of those who lived in tents on the east of Nobah and Jogbehah, and struck the army; for the army felt secure.19✦ 12 Zebah and Zalmunna fled and he pursued them. He took the two kings of Midian, Zebah and Zalmunna, and confused all the army.20✦ 13 Gideon the son of Joash returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres.21✦ 14 He caught a young man22 of the men of Succoth, and inquired of him; and he described for him the princes of Succoth, and its elders, seventy-seven men.23✦ 15 He came to the men of Succoth, and said, “See Zebah and Zalmunna, concerning whom you taunted me, saying, ‘Are the hands of Zebah and Zalmunna now in your hand, that we should give bread to your men who are weary?’”24✦ 16 He took the elders of the city, and thorns of the wilderness and briers, and with them he taught the men of Succoth.25✦ 17 He broke down the tower of Penuel, and killed the men of the city.26✦ 18 Then he said to Zebah and Zalmunna, “What kind of men were they whom you killed at Tabor?” They answered, “They were like you. They all resembled the children of a king.”27✦ 19 He said, “They were my brothers, the sons of my mother. As Yahweh lives, if you had saved them alive, I would not kill you.”2829✦ 20 He said to Jether his firstborn, “Get up and kill them!” But the youth didn’t draw his sword; for he was afraid, because he was yet a youth.30✦ 21 Then Zebah and Zalmunna said, “You rise and fall on us; for as the man31 is, so is his strength.” Gideon arose, and killed Zebah and Zalmunna, and took the crescents that were on their camels’ necks.32✦ 22 Then the men of Israel said to Gideon, “Rule over us, both you, your son, and your son’s son also; for you have saved us out of the hand of Midian.”33✦ 23 Gideon said to them, “I will not rule over you, neither shall my son rule over you. Yahweh shall rule over you34.”3536✦ 24 Gideon said to them, “I do have a request: that you would each give me the earrings of his plunder.” (For they had golden earrings, because they were Ishmaelites.)3738✦ 25 They answered, “We will willingly give them.” They spread a garment, and every man39 threw the earrings of his plunder into it.40 26 The weight of the golden earrings that he requested was one thousand and seven hundred shekels of gold, in addition to the crescents, and the pendants, and the purple clothing that was on the kings of Midian, and in addition to the chains that were about their camels’ necks.41✦ 27 Gideon made an ephod out of it, and put it in Ophrah, his city. Then all Israel played the prostitute with it42 there; and it became a snare to Gideon and to his house.43✦ 28 So Midian was subdued before the children of Israel, and they lifted up their heads no more. The land had rest forty years in the days of Gideon.44 29 Jerubbaal the son of Joash went and lived in his own house.45✦ 30 Gideon had seventy sons conceived from his body, for he had many wives.46 31 His concubine who was in Shechem also bore him a son, and he named him Abimelech.47 32 Gideon the son of Joash died in a good48 old age, and was buried in the tomb of Joash his father, in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.4950 33 As soon as Gideon was dead, the children of Israel turned again and played the prostitute following the Baals, and made Baal Berith their god51.5253✦ 34 The children of Israel didn’t remember Yahweh their God54, who had delivered them out of the hand of all their enemies on every side;5556✦ 35 neither did they show kindness to the house of Jerubbaal, that is, Gideon, according to all the goodness which he had shown to Israel.

9

1✦1 Abimelech the son of Jerubbaal went to Shechem to his mother’s brothers, and spoke with them and with all the family of the house of his mother’s father, saying,2✦ 2 “Please speak in the ears of all the men of Shechem, ‘Is it better for you that all the sons of Jerubbaal, who are seventy persons, rule over you, or that one rule over you?’ Remember also that I am your bone and your flesh.”3 3 His mother’s brothers spoke of him in the ears of all the men of Shechem all these words. Their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech; for they said, “He is our brother.”4 4 They gave him seventy pieces of silver out of the house of Baal Berith, with which Abimelech hired vain and reckless fellows who followed him.56✦ 5 He went to his father’s house at Ophrah, and killed his brothers the sons of Jerubbaal, being seventy persons, on one stone; but Jotham the youngest son of Jerubbaal was left, for he hid himself.78✦ 6 All the men of Shechem assembled themselves together with all the house of Millo, and went and made Abimelech king by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.9✦ 7 When they told it to Jotham, he went and stood on the top of Mount Gerizim and lifted up his voice, cried out, and said to them, “Listen to me, you men of Shechem, that God10 may listen to you.11✦ 8 The trees set out to anoint a king12 over themselves. They said to the olive tree, ‘Reign over us.’13✦ 9 “But the olive tree said to them, ‘Should I stop producing my oil, with which they honor God14 and man15 by me, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’16✦ 10 “The trees said to the fig tree, ‘Come and reign over us.’17✦ 11 “But the fig tree said to them, ‘Should I leave my sweetness, and my good18 fruit, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’19✦ 12 “The trees said to the vine, ‘Come and reign over us.’20✦ 13 “The vine said to them, ‘Should I leave my new wine, which cheers God21 and man22, and go to wave back and forth over the trees?’23✦ 14 “Then all the trees said to the bramble, ‘Come and reign over us.’2425✦ 15 “The bramble said to the trees, ‘If in truth you anoint me king over you, then come and take refuge in my shade; and if not, let fire come out of the bramble, and devour the cedars of Lebanon.’26✦ 16 “Now therefore, if you have dealt truly and righteously, in that you have made Abimelech king, and if you have dealt well with Jerubbaal and his house, and have done to him according to the deserving of his hands27✦ 17 (for my father fought for you, risked his life, and delivered you out of the hand of Midian;28✦ 18 and you have risen up against my father’s house today and have slain his sons, seventy persons, on one stone, and have made Abimelech, the son of his female servant, king over the men of Shechem, because he is your brother);29✦ 19 if you then have dealt truly and righteously with Jerubbaal and with his house today, then rejoice in Abimelech, and let him also rejoice in you;30✦ 20 but if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the men of Shechem and the house of Millo; and let fire come out from the men of Shechem and from the house of Millo and devour Abimelech.”31✦ 21 Jotham ran away and fled, and went to Beer and lived there, for fear32 of Abimelech his brother.33✦ 22 Abimelech was prince over Israel three years.34 23 Then God35 sent an evil spirit36 between Abimelech and the men of Shechem; and the men of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,37 24 that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and that their blood38 might be laid on Abimelech their brother who killed them, and on the men of Shechem who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.39✦ 25 The men of Shechem set an ambush for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who came along that way by them; and Abimelech was told about it.40✦ 26 Gaal the son of Ebed came with his brothers and went over to Shechem; and the men of Shechem put their trust in him.414243 27 They went out into the field, harvested their vineyards, trod the grapes, celebrated, and went into the house of their god44 and ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.45✦ 28 Gaal the son of Ebed said, “Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him? Isn’t he the son of Jerubbaal? Isn’t Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem, but why should we serve him?4647 29 I wish that this people were under my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech.” He said to Abimelech, “Increase your army and come out!”4849 30 When Zebul the ruler of the city heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed, his anger burned.50 31 He sent messengers to Abimelech craftily, saying, “Behold, Gaal the son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem; and behold, they incite the city against you.51✦ 32 Now therefore, go up by night, you and the people who are with you, and lie in wait in the field.52 33 It shall be that in the morning, as soon as the sun is up, you shall rise early and rush on the city. Behold, when he and the people who are with him come out against you, then may you do to them as you shall find occasion.”53✦ 34 Abimelech rose up, and all the people who were with him, by night, and they laid wait against Shechem in four companies.54✦ 35 Gaal the son of Ebed went out, and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city. Abimelech rose up, and the people who were with him, from the ambush.55 36 When Gaal saw the people, he said to Zebul, “Behold, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains.” Zebul said to him, “You see the shadows of the mountains as if they were men.”56 37 Gaal spoke again and said, “Behold, people are coming down by the middle of the land57, and one company comes by the way of the oak of Meonenim.”5859 38 Then Zebul said to him, “Now where is your mouth, that you said, ‘Who is Abimelech, that we should serve him?’ Isn’t this the people that you have despised? Please go out now and fight with them.”60 39 Gaal went out before the men of Shechem, and fought with Abimelech.61 40 Abimelech chased him, and he fled before him, and many fell wounded, even to the entrance of the gate.62 41 Abimelech lived at Arumah; and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers, that they should not dwell in Shechem.6364 42 On the next day, the people went out into the field; and they told Abimelech.65 43 He took the people and divided them into three companies, and laid wait in the field; and he looked, and behold, the people came out of the city. So, he rose up against them and struck them.66✦ 44 Abimelech and the companies that were with him rushed forward and stood in the entrance of the gate of the city; and the two companies rushed on all who were in the field and struck them.67✦ 45 Abimelech fought against the city all that day; and he took the city and killed the people in it. He beat down the city and sowed it with salt.68✦ 46 When all the men of the tower of Shechem heard of it, they entered into the stronghold of the house of Elberith.6970✦ 47 Abimelech was told that all the men of the tower of Shechem were gathered together.71 48 Abimelech went up to Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who were with him; and Abimelech took an ax in his hand, and cut down a bough from the trees, and took it up, and laid it on his shoulder. Then he said to the people who were with him, “What you have seen me do, make haste, and do as I have done!”7273 49 All the people likewise each cut down his bough, followed Abimelech, and put them at the base of the stronghold, and set the stronghold on fire over them, so that all the people of the tower of Shechem died also, about a thousand men and women.7475✦ 50 Then Abimelech went to Thebez and encamped against Thebez, and took it.7677✦ 51 But there was a strong tower within the city, and all the men and women of the city fled there, and shut themselves in, and went up to the roof of the tower.78✦ 52 Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and came near to the door of the tower to burn it with fire.79 53 A certain woman80 cast an upper millstone on Abimelech’s head81, and broke his skull.82✦ 54 Then he called hastily to the young man83, his armor bearer, and said to him, “Draw your sword and kill me, that men not say of me, ‘A woman84 killed him.’ His young man thrust him through, and he died.”8586✦ 55 When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they each departed to his place.8788 56 Thus God89 repaid the wickedness of Abimelech, which he did to his father in killing his seventy brothers;90✦ 57 and God91 repaid all the wickedness of the men of Shechem on their heads; and the curse of Jotham the son of Jerubbaal came on them.

11 After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man2 of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.34✦ 2 He judged Israel twenty-three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.5 3 After him Jair, the Gileadite, arose. He judged Israel twenty-two years.6✦ 4 He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts7. They had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land8 of Gilead.9✦ 5 Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.1011 6 The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned Yahweh, and didn’t serve him.121314✦ 7 Yahweh’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.1516✦ 8 They troubled and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the children of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land17 of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.18✦ 9 The children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was very distressed.19✦ 10 The children of Israel cried to Yahweh, saying, “We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our God20, and have served the Baals.”2122✦ 11 Yahweh said to the children of Israel, “Didn’t I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?2324 12 The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand.25✦ 13 Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more.26✦ 14 Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress!”27✦ 15 The children of Israel said to Yahweh, “We have sinned!28 Do to us whatever seems good29 to you; only deliver us, please, today.”3031✦ 16 They put away the foreign gods from among them and served Yahweh; and his soul32 was grieved for the misery of Israel.3334✦ 17 Then the children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead. The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.35✦ 18 The people, the princes of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man36 who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

11

1✦1 Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man2 of valor. He was the son of a prostitute3. Gilead became the father of Jephthah.45✦ 2 Gilead’s wife bore him sons. When his wife’s sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, “You will not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman6.”7✦ 3 Then Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land8 of Tob. Outlaws joined up with Jephthah, and they went out with him.910 4 After a while, the children of Ammon made war against Israel.11✦ 5 When the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah out of the land12 of Tob.13✦ 6 They said to Jephthah, “Come and be our chief, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.”14✦ 7 Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Didn’t you hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”15✦ 8 The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “Therefore we have turned again to you now, that you may go with us and fight with the children of Ammon. You will be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”16✦ 9 Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me home again to fight with the children of Ammon, and Yahweh delivers them before me, will I be your head?”1718✦ 10 The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “Yahweh will be witness between us. Surely we will do what you say.”1920✦ 11 Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over them. Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.2122✦ 12 Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, “What do you have to do with me, that you have come to me to fight against my land23?”24✦ 13 The king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah, “Because Israel took away my land25 when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now therefore restore that territory again peaceably.”26✦ 14 Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the children of Ammon;27✦ 15 and he said to him, “Jephthah says: Israel didn’t take away the land28 of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon;29✦ 16 but when they came up from Egypt, and Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh,30✦ 17 then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land31;’ but the king of Edom didn’t listen. In the same way, he sent to the king of Moab, but he refused; so Israel stayed in Kadesh.32✦ 18 Then they went through the wilderness, and went around the land33 of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they didn’t come within the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.34✦ 19 Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land35 to my place.’36✦ 20 But Sihon didn’t trust Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.37✦ 21 Yahweh, the God38 of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel possessed all the land39 of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.4041✦ 22 They possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even to the Jordan.42✦ 23 So now Yahweh, the God43 of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and should you possess them?4445✦ 24 Won’t you possess that which Chemosh your god46 gives you to possess? So whoever Yahweh our God has dispossessed from before us, them will we possess.4748✦ 25 Now are you anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them?49✦ 26 Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities that are along the side of the Arnon for three hundred years! Why didn’t you recover them within that time?50✦ 27 Therefore I have not sinned against you, but you do me wrong to war against me. May Yahweh the Judge be judge today between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”5152✦ 28 However, the king of the children of Ammon didn’t listen to the words of Jephthah which he sent him.53✦ 29 Then Yahweh’s Spirit54 came on Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed over to the children of Ammon.5556✦ 30 Jephthah vowed a vow to Yahweh57, and said, “If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,585960✦ 31 then it shall be, that whatever comes out of the doors61 of my house to meet me when I return in peace62 from the children of Ammon, it shall be Yahweh’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.”6364✦ 32 So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Yahweh delivered them into his hand.6566✦ 33 He struck them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and to Abelcheramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.67686970✦ 34 Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house; and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She was his only child. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter.71✦ 35 When he saw her, he tore his clothes, and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are one of those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to Yahweh, and I can’t go back.”7273✦ 36 She said to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to Yahweh; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of your mouth, because Yahweh has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, even on the children of Ammon.”7475✦ 37 Then she said to her father, “Let this thing be done for me. Leave me alone two months, that I may depart and go down on the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.”76✦ 38 He said, “Go.” He sent her away for two months; and she departed, she and her companions, and mourned her virginity on the mountains.77✦ 39 At the end of two months, she returned to her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed. She was a virgin. It became a custom in Israel7879 40 that the daughters of Israel went yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

11 The men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward; and they said to Jephthah, “Why did you pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didn’t call us to go with you? We will burn your house around you with fire2!”34✦ 2 Jephthah said to them, “I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, you didn’t save me out of their hand.5✦ 3 When I saw that you didn’t save me, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and Yahweh delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me today, to fight against me?”67✦ 4 Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought with Ephraim. The men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they said, “You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the middle of Ephraim, and in the middle of Manasseh.”8✦ 5 The Gileadites took the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. Whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, “Let me go over,” the men of Gilead said to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he said, “No;”9✦ 6 then they said to him, “Now say ‘Shibboleth10;’” and he said “Sibboleth”; for he couldn’t manage to pronounce it correctly, then they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.11✦ 7 Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and was buried in the cities of Gilead.12 8 After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.1314✦ 9 He had thirty sons. He sent his thirty daughters outside his clan, and he brought in thirty daughters from outside his clan for his sons. He judged Israel seven years.15 10 Ibzan died, and was buried at Bethlehem.16 11 After him, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.1718✦ 12 Elon the Zebulunite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.19✦ 13 After him, Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.20212223✦ 14 He had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons who rode on seventy donkey colts. He judged Israel eight years.24✦ 15 Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land25 of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

123✦1 The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight; and Yahweh delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.456✦ 2 There was a certain man7 of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and childless.8✦ 3 Yahweh’s angel appeared to the woman9, and said to her, “See now, you are barren and childless; but you shall conceive and bear a son.101112 4 Now therefore please beware and drink no wine nor strong drink, and don’t eat any unclean thing;1314 5 for, behold, you shall conceive and give birth to a son. No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God15 from the womb16. He shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”17✦ 6 Then the woman1819 came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God20 came to me, and his face was like the face of the angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he was from, neither did he tell me his name;21 7 but he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. Don’t eat any unclean thing, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God22 from the womb to the day of his death.’”23 8 Then Manoah entreated Yahweh, and said, “Oh, Lord, please let the man24 of God25 whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we should do to the child who shall be born.”2627✦ 9 God28 listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman29 as she sat in the field; but Manoah, her husband, wasn’t with her.30 10 The woman3132 hurried and ran, and told her husband, saying to him, “Behold, the man who came to me that day has appeared to me.”33✦ 11 Manoah arose and followed his wife, and came to the man34, and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” He said, “I am.”3536 12 Manoah said, “Now let your words happen. What shall the child’s way of life and mission be?”37 13 Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Of all that I said to the woman38 let her beware.3940 14 She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. Let her observe all that I commanded her.”41✦ 15 Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “Please stay with us, that we may make a young goat ready for you.”4243✦ 16 Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I won’t eat your bread. If you will prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to Yahweh.” For Manoah didn’t know that he was Yahweh’s angel.4445✦ 17 Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “What is your name, that when your words happen, we may honor you?”4647✦ 18 Yahweh’s angel said to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible48?”4950✦ 19 So Manoah took the young goat with the meal offering, and offered it on the rock to Yahweh. Then the angel did an amazing thing as Manoah and his wife watched.5152✦ 20 For when the flame went up toward the sky from off the altar, Yahweh’s angel ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife watched; and they fell on their faces to the ground53.545556✦ 21 But Yahweh’s angel didn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah knew that he was Yahweh’s angel.5758✦ 22 Manoah said to his wife, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God59.”60✦ 23 But his wife said to him, “If Yahweh were pleased to kill us, he wouldn’t have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand, and he wouldn’t have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us such things as these at this time.”6162 24 The woman63 bore a son and named him Samson. 12✦1 Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman3 in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.4✦ 2 He came up, and told his father and his mother, saying, “I have seen a woman5 in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines. Now therefore get her for me as my wife.”6✦ 3 Then his father and his mother said to him, “Isn’t there a woman7 among your brothers’ daughters, or among all my people, that you go to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson said to his father, “Get her for me, for she pleases me well.”8✦ 4 But his father and his mother didn’t know that it was of Yahweh; for he sought an occasion against the Philistines. He came to his father and mother and gave to them, and they ate, but he didn’t tell them that he had taken the honey out of the lion’s body.19 10 His father went down to the woman20; and Samson made a feast there, for the young men used to do so.21✦ 11 When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.22✦ 12 Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle now. If you can tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing;2324✦ 13 but if you can’t tell me the answer, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.” They said to him, “Tell us your riddle, that we may hear it.”25 14 He said to them, “Out of the eater came out food26. Out of the strong came out sweetness.” They couldn’t in three days declare the riddle.27 15 On the seventh day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband, that he may declare to us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you called us to impoverish us? Isn’t that so?”28✦ 16 Samson’s wife wept before him, and said, “You just hate me, and don’t love me. You’ve told a riddle to the children of my people, and haven’t told it to me.” He said to her, “Behold, I haven’t told my father or my mother, so why should I tell you?”29✦ 17 She wept before him the seven days, while their feast lasted; and on the seventh day, he told her, because she pressed him severely; and she told the riddle to the children of her people.30✦ 18 The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” He said to them, “If you hadn’t plowed with my heifer, you wouldn’t have found out my riddle.”31✦ 19 Yahweh’s Spirit32 came mightily on him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of them. He took their plunder, then gave the changes of clothing to those who declared the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.3334✦ 20 But Samson’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.

She said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He broke the cords as a flax thread is broken when it touches the fire. So his strength was not known.1516 10 Delilah said to Samson, “Behold, you have mocked me, and told me lies. Now please tell me how you might be bound.”17✦ 11 He said to her, “If they only bind me with new ropes with which no work has been done, then shall I become weak, and be as another man18.”19✦ 12 So Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them, then said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” The ambush was waiting in the inner room. He broke them off his arms like a thread.20 13 Delilah said to Samson, “Until now, you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me with what you might be bound.” He said to her, “If you weave the seven locks of my head with the fabric on the loom.”21 14 She fastened it with the pin, and said to him, “The Philistines are on you, Samson!” He awakened out of his sleep, and plucked away the pin of the beam and the fabric.22 15 She said to him, “How can you say, ‘I love23 you,’ when your heart24 is not with me? The lords of the Philistines gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god40, and to rejoice; for they said, “Our god has delivered Samson our enemy into our hand.”4142✦ 24 When the people saw him, they praised their god43; for they said, “Our god has delivered our enemy and the destroyer of our country, who has slain many of us, into our hand.”44✦ 25 When their hearts were merry, they said, “Call for Samson, that he may entertain us.” They called for Samson out of the prison; and he performed before them. They set him between the pillars;45✦ 26 and Samson said to the boy who held him by the hand, “Allow me to feel the pillars on which the house rests, that I may lean on them.”4647 27 Now the house was full of men and women; and all the lords of the Philistines were there; and there were on the roof about three thousand men and women, who saw while Samson performed.48 28 Samson called to Yahweh, and said, “Lord Yahweh, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, only this once, God, that I may be at once avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes.”495051✦ 29 Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the house rested and leaned on them, the one with his right hand and the other with his left.52✦ 30 Samson said, “Let me die with the Philistines5354!” He bowed himself with all his might; and the house fell on the lords, and on all the people who were in it. So the dead that he killed at his death were more than those who he killed in his life.55✦ 31 Then his brothers and all the house of his father came down and took him, and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial site of Manoah his father. He judged Israel twenty years.

121 In those days there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites sought an inheritance to dwell in; for to that day, their inheritance had not fallen to them among the tribes of Israel.✦ 2 The children of Dan sent five men of their family from their whole number, men of valor, from Zorah and from Eshtaol, to spy out the land3 and to search it. They said to them, “Go, explore the land!” They came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and lodged there.4✦ 3 When they were by the house of Micah, they knew the voice of the young man5 the Levite; so they went over there and said to him, “Who brought you here? What do you have here?”6 4 He said to them, “Thus and thus has Micah dealt with me, and he has hired me, and I have become his priest.”7 5 They said to him, “Please ask counsel of God8, that we may know whether our way which we go shall be prosperous.”910 6 The priest said to them, “Go in peace11. Your way in which you go is before Yahweh.”1213 7 Then the five men departed and came to Laish and saw the people who were there, how they lived in safety14, in the way of the Sidonians, quiet and secure; for there was no one in the land15 possessing authority, that might put them to shame in anything, and they were far from the Sidonians, and had no dealings with anyone else.161718✦ 8 They came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol; and their brothers asked them, “What do you say?”19✦ 9 They said, “Arise, and let’s go up against them; for we have seen the land20, and behold, it is very good21. 1✦1 In those days, when there was no king in Israel, there was a certain Levite living on the farther side of the hill country of Ephraim, who took for himself a concubine out of Bethlehem Judah.2✦ 2 His concubine played the prostitute against him, and went away from him to her father’s house to Bethlehem Judah, and was there for four months.3 3 Her husband arose and went after her to speak kindly to her, to bring her again, having his servant with him and a couple of donkeys. Then the young lady’s father said to the man8, “Please be pleased to stay all night, and let your heart9 be merry.”10 7 The man11 rose up to depart; but his father-in-law urged him, and he stayed there again.12 8 He arose early in the morning on the fifth day to depart; and the young lady’s father said, “Please strengthen your heart13 and stay until the day declines;” and they both ate.14✦ 9 When the man15 rose up to depart, he, and his concubine, and his servant, his father-in-law, the young lady’s father, said to him, “Behold, now the day draws toward evening, please stay all night. I am going to Yahweh’s house; and there is no one who has taken me into his house.293031 19 Yet there is both straw and feed for our donkeys; and there is bread and wine also for me, and for your servant, and for the young man32 who is with your servants. Then they washed their feet, and ate and drank.37✦ 22 As they were making their hearts merry, behold, the men of the city, certain wicked fellows38, surrounded the house, beating at the door; and they spoke to the master of the house, the old man39, saying, “Bring out the man who came into your house, that we can have sex with him!”40 23 The man41, the master of the house, went out to them, and said to them, “No, my brothers, please don’t act so wickedly; since this man has come into my house, don’t do this folly.42✦ 24 Behold, here is my virgin daughter and his concubine. When the day began to dawn, they let her go.47 26 Then the woman4849 came in the dawning of the day, and fell down at the door of the man’s house where her lord50 was, until it was light51.52 27 Her lord53 rose up in the morning and opened the doors of the house, and went out to go his way; and behold, the woman54 his concubine had fallen down at the door of the house, with her hands on the threshold.55 28 He said to her, “Get up, and let’s get going!” but no one answered. Then he took her up on the donkey; and the man56 rose up, and went to his place.57 29 When he had come into his house, he took a knife and cut up his concubine, and divided her58, limb by limb, into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the borders of Israel.59✦ 30 It was so, that all who saw it said, “Such a deed has not been done or seen from the day that the children of Israel came up out of the land60 of Egypt to this day! 11 Then all the children of Israel went out, and the congregation was assembled as one man2, from Dan even to Beersheba, with the land3 of Gilead, to Yahweh at Mizpah.45✦ 2 The chiefs of all the people, even of all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God6, four hundred thousand footmen who drew sword.7✦ 3 (Now the children of Benjamin heard that the children of Israel had gone up to Mizpah.) Every one of them could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.1617✦ 17 The men of Israel, besides Benjamin, were counted four hundred thousand men who drew sword. All these were men of war.✦ 18 The children of Israel arose, went up to Bethel, and asked counsel of God18. They asked, “Who shall go up for us first to battle against the children of Benjamin?” Yahweh said, “Judah first.”1920✦ 19 The children of Israel rose up in the morning and encamped against Gibeah.✦ 20 The men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin; and the men of Israel set the battle in array against them at Gibeah.✦ 21 The children of Benjamin came out of Gibeah, and on that day destroyed twenty-two thousand of the Israelite men down to the ground21.22✦ 22 The people, the men of Israel, encouraged themselves, and set the battle again in array in the place where they set themselves in array the first day.✦ 23 The children of Israel went up and wept before Yahweh until evening; and they asked of Yahweh, saying, “Shall I again draw near to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother?” Yahweh said, “Go up against him.”2324✦ 24 The children of Israel came near against the children of Benjamin the second day.✦ 25 Benjamin went out against them out of Gibeah the second day, and destroyed down to the ground25 of the children of Israel again eighteen thousand men. All these drew the sword.✦ 26 Then all the children of Israel and all the people went up, and came to Bethel, and wept, and sat there before Yahweh, and fasted that day until evening; then they offered burnt offerings and peace26 offerings before Yahweh.272829✦ 27 The children of Israel asked Yahweh (for the ark of the covenant30 of God31 was there in those days,3233✦ 28 and Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron, stood before it in those days), saying, “Shall I yet again go out to battle against the children of Benjamin my brother, or shall I cease?” Yahweh said, “Go up; for tomorrow I will deliver him into your hand.”3435✦ 29 Israel set ambushes all around Gibeah.36✦ 30 The children of Israel went up against the children of Benjamin on the third day, and set themselves in array against Gibeah, as at other times.37✦ 31 The children of Benjamin went out against the people, and were drawn away from the city; and they began to strike and kill of the people as at other times, in the highways, of which one goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah, in the field, about thirty men of Israel.3839✦ 32 The children of Benjamin said, “They are struck down before us, as at the first.” But the children of Israel said, “Let’s flee, and draw them away from the city to the highways.”40✦ 33 All the men of Israel rose up out of their place and set themselves in array at Baal Tamar. Then the ambushers of Israel broke out of their place, even out of Maareh Geba.4142✦ 34 Ten thousand chosen men out of all Israel came over against Gibeah, and the battle was severe; but they didn’t know that disaster was close to them.43✦ 35 Yahweh struck Benjamin before Israel; and the children of Israel destroyed of Benjamin that day twenty-five thousand one hundred men. 1✦1 Naomi had a relative of her husband’s, a mighty man2 of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.3✦ 2 Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Let me now go to the field, and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor.” She said to her, “Go, my daughter.”4✦ 3 She went, and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz5, who was of the family of Elimelech.67✦ 4 Behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers, “May Yahweh be with you.” They answered him, “May Yahweh bless you.”8910✦ 5 Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, “Whose young lady is this?”11✦ 6 The servant who was set over the reapers answered, “It is the Moabite lady who came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.12✦ 7 She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”13 8 Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. She ate, was satisfied, and left some of it.29✦ 15 When she had risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don’t reproach her.30 16 Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it. Where have you worked? Only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli thought she was drunk.36✦ 14 Eli said to her, “How long will you be drunk? Get rid of your wine!”37 15 Hannah answered, “No, my lord38, I am a woman39 of a sorrowful spirit40. I have not been drinking wine or strong drink, but I poured out my soul41 before Yahweh.42✦ 16 Don’t consider your servant a wicked woman; for I have been speaking out of the abundance of my complaint and my provocation.”43 17 Then Eli answered, “Go in peace44; and may the God45 of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of him.”46 18 She said, “Let your servant find favor in your sight.” So the woman47 went her way and ate; and her facial expression wasn’t sad any more.48 19 They rose up in the morning early and worshiped Yahweh, then returned and came to their house to Ramah. Then Elkanah knew Hannah his wife; and Yahweh remembered her.4950 20 When the time had come, Hannah conceived, and bore a son; and she named him Samuel, saying, “Because I have asked him of Yahweh.”515253 21 The man54 Elkanah, and all his house, went up to offer to Yahweh the yearly sacrifice and his vow.5556✦ 22 But Hannah didn’t go up, for she said to her husband, “Not until the child is weaned; then I will bring him, that he may appear before Yahweh, and stay there forever.”5758✦ 23 Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems good59 to you. Wait until you have weaned him; only may Yahweh establish his word.” So the woman60 waited and nursed her son until she weaned him.6162 24 When she had weaned him, she took him up with her, with three bulls, and one ephah of meal, and a container of wine, and brought him to Yahweh’s house in Shiloh. The child was young.6364✦ 25 They killed the bull, and brought the child to Eli.65 26 She said, “Oh, my lord66, as your soul67 lives, my lord, I am the woman68 who stood by you here, praying to Yahweh.69✦ 27 I prayed for this child70, and Yahweh has given me my petition which I asked of him.7172✦ 28 Therefore I have also given him to Yahweh. As long as he lives he is given to Yahweh.” He worshiped Yahweh there.

2

12✦1 Hannah prayed, and said, “My heart3 exults in Yahweh4! My horn is exalted in Yahweh. My mouth is enlarged over my enemies, because I rejoice in your salvation5.6789✦ 2 There is no one as holy10 as Yahweh, for there is no one besides you, nor is there any rock like our God11.1213141516✦ 3 “Don’t keep talking so exceedingly proudly. Don’t let arrogance come out of your mouth, for Yahweh is a God17 of knowledge. By him actions are weighed.1819✦ 4 “The bows of the mighty men are broken. Those who stumbled are armed with strength.20✦ 5 Those who were full have hired themselves out for bread. Those who were hungry are satisfied. Yes, the barren has borne seven. She who has many children languishes.21✦ 6 “Yahweh kills and makes alive22. He brings down to Sheol and brings up.232425✦ 7 Yahweh makes poor and makes rich. He brings low, he also lifts up.262728✦ 8 He raises up the poor out of the dust29. He lifts up the needy from the dunghill to make them sit with princes and inherit the throne of glory30. For the pillars of the earth31 are Yahweh’s. He has set the world on them.32333435✦ 9 He will keep the feet of his holy ones, but the wicked will be put to silence in darkness36; for no man37 will prevail by strength.38✦ 10 Those who strive with Yahweh shall be broken to pieces. He will thunder against them in the sky. “Yahweh will judge the ends of the earth39. He will give strength to his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed40.”414243✦ 11 Elkanah went to Ramah to his house. The child served Yahweh before Eli the priest.4445 12 Now the sons of Eli were wicked men46. They didn’t know Yahweh.4748✦ 13 The custom of the priests with the people was that when anyone offered a sacrifice, the priest’s servant came while the meat was boiling, with a fork of three teeth in his hand;4950✦ 14 and he stabbed it into the pan, or kettle, or cauldron, or pot. The priest took all that the fork brought up for himself. They did this to all the Israelites who came there to Shiloh.5152✦ 15 Yes, before they burned the fat, the priest’s servant came, and said to the man53 who sacrificed, “Give meat to roast for the priest; for he will not accept boiled meat from you, but raw.”54✦ 16 If the man55 said to him, “Let the fat be burned first, and then take as much as your soul56 desires;” then he would say, “No, but you shall give it to me now; and if not, I will take it by force.”57✦ 17 The sin58 of the young men was very great before Yahweh; for the men despised Yahweh’s offering.5960✦ 18 But Samuel ministered before Yahweh, being a child, clothed with a linen ephod.6162✦ 19 Moreover his mother made him a little robe, and brought it to him from year to year when she came up with her husband to offer the yearly sacrifice.63✦ 20 Eli blessed Elkanah and his wife, and said, “May Yahweh give you offspring from this woman64 for the petition which was asked of Yahweh.” Then they went to their own home.6566 21 Yahweh visited Hannah, and she conceived and bore three sons and two daughters. The child Samuel grew before Yahweh.6768 22 Now Eli was very old; and he heard all that his sons did to all Israel, and how that they slept with the women who served at the door of the Tent of Meeting.69✦ 23 He said to them, “Why do you do such things? For I hear of your evil dealings from all these people.70✦ 24 No, my sons; for it is not a good71 report that I hear! You make Yahweh’s people disobey.7273✦ 25 If one man74 sin75s against another, God will judge him; but if a man sins against Yahweh, who will intercede for him?” Notwithstanding, they didn’t listen to the voice of their father, because Yahweh intended to kill them.7677✦ 26 The child Samuel grew on, and increased in favor both with Yahweh and also with men.787980✦ 27 A man81 of God82 came to Eli and said to him, “Yahweh says, ‘Did I reveal myself to the house of your father when they were in Egypt in bondage to Pharaoh’s house?8384✦ 28 Didn’t I choose him out of all the tribes of Israel to be my priest, to go up to my altar, to burn incense, to wear an ephod before me? Didn’t I give to the house of your father all the offerings of the children of Israel made by fire?85✦ 29 Why do you kick at my sacrifice and at my offering, which I have commanded in my habitation, and honor your sons above me, to make yourselves fat with the best of all the offerings of Israel my people?’86✦ 30 “Therefore Yahweh, the God87 of Israel, says, ‘I said indeed that your house and the house of your father should walk before me forever.’ But now Yahweh says, ‘Far be it from me; for those who honor me I will honor, and those who despise me will be cursed.888990✦ 31 Behold, the days come that I will cut off your arm and the arm of your father’s house, that there will not be an old man91 in your house.92✦ 32 You will see the affliction of my habitation, in all the wealth which I will give Israel. There shall not be an old man93 in your house forever.9495✦ 33 The man96 of yours whom I don’t cut off from my altar will consume your eyes and grieve your heart97. All the increase of your house will die in the flower of their age.98✦ 34 This will be the sign to you that will come on your two sons, on Hophni and Phinehas: in one day they will both die.99✦ 35 I will raise up a faithful priest for myself who will do according to that which is in my heart100 and in my mind. I will build him a sure house. He will walk before my anointed101 forever.102✦ 36 It will happen that everyone who is left in your house will come and bow down to him for a piece of silver and a loaf of bread, and will say, “Please put me into one of the priests’ offices, that I may eat a morsel of bread.”’”

3

1✦1 The child Samuel ministered to Yahweh before Eli. Yahweh’s word was rare in those days23. There were not many visions, then.456✦ 2 At that time, when Eli was laid down in his place (now his eyes had begun to grow dim, so that he could not see),7✦ 3 and God8’s lamp hadn’t yet gone out, and Samuel had laid down in Yahweh’s temple where God’s ark was,910✦ 4 Yahweh called Samuel. He said, “Here I am.”1112✦ 5 He ran to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” He said, “I didn’t call. Lie down again.” He went and lay down.13✦ 6 Yahweh called yet again, “Samuel!” Samuel arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” He answered, “I didn’t call, my son. Lie down again.”1415✦ 7 Now Samuel didn’t yet know Yahweh, neither was Yahweh’s word yet revealed to him.1617✦ 8 Yahweh called Samuel again the third time. He arose and went to Eli and said, “Here I am; for you called me.” Eli perceived that Yahweh had called the child.1819✦ 9 Therefore Eli said to Samuel, “Go, lie down. It shall be, if he calls you, that you shall say, ‘Speak, Yahweh; for your servant hears.’” So Samuel went and lay down in his place.2021✦ 10 Yahweh came, and stood, and called as at other times, “Samuel! Samuel!” Then Samuel said, “Speak; for your servant hears22.”2324✦ 11 Yahweh said to Samuel, “Behold, I will do a thing in Israel at which both the ears of everyone who hears it will tingle.2526✦ 12 In that day I will perform against Eli all that I have spoken concerning his house, from the beginning even to the end.27✦ 13 For I have told him that I will judge his house forever for the iniquity which he knew, because his sons brought a curse on themselves, and he didn’t restrain them.28✦ 14 Therefore I have sworn to the house of Eli that the iniquity of Eli’s house shall not be removed with sacrifice or offering forever.”29✦ 15 Samuel lay until the morning, and opened the doors of Yahweh’s house. Samuel was afraid to show Eli the vision.3031✦ 16 Then Eli called Samuel and said, “Samuel, my son!” He said, “Here I am.”32 17 He said, “What is the thing that he has spoken to you? Please don’t hide it from me. God33 do so to you, and more also, if you hide anything from me of all the things that he spoke to you.”3435✦ 18 Samuel told him every bit, and hid nothing from him. He said, “It is Yahweh. Let him do what seems good36 to him.”3738✦ 19 Samuel grew, and Yahweh was with him and let none of his words fall to the ground39.4041✦ 20 All Israel from Dan even to Beersheba knew that Samuel was established to be a prophet of Yahweh.4243✦ 21 Yahweh appeared again in Shiloh; for Yahweh revealed himself to Samuel in Shiloh by Yahweh’s word.

4

12✦1 The word of Samuel came to all Israel. Now Israel went out against the Philistines to battle, and encamped beside Ebenezer; and the Philistines encamped in Aphek.34✦ 2 The Philistines put themselves in array against Israel. When they joined battle, Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who killed about four thousand men of the army in the field.5✦ 3 When the people had come into the camp, the elders of Israel said, “Why has Yahweh defeated us today before the Philistines? Let’s get the ark of Yahweh’s covenant6 out of Shiloh and bring it to us, that it may come among us and save us out of the hand of our enemies.”78✦ 4 So the people sent to Shiloh, and they brought from there the ark of the covenant9 of Yahweh of Armies, who sits above the cherubim; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God10.1112✦ 5 When the ark of Yahweh’s covenant13 came into the camp, all Israel shouted with a great shout, so that the earth14 resounded.1516✦ 6 When the Philistines heard the noise of the shout, they said, “What does the noise of this great shout in the camp of the Hebrews mean?” They understood that Yahweh’s ark had come into the camp.1718✦ 7 The Philistines were afraid, for they said, “God19 has come into the camp.” They said, “Woe to us! For there has not been such a thing before.20✦ 8 Woe to us! Who shall deliver us out of the hand of these mighty gods? These are the gods that struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.21✦ 9 Be strong and behave like men, O you Philistines, that you not be servants to the Hebrews, as they have been to you. Strengthen yourselves like men, and fight!”22✦ 10 The Philistines fought, and Israel was defeated, and each man23 fled to his tent. There was a very great slaughter; for thirty thousand footmen of Israel fell.24✦ 11 God25’s ark was taken; and the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were slain.26✦ 12 A man27 of Benjamin ran out of the army and came to Shiloh the same day, with his clothes torn and with dirt on his head.2829 13 When he came, behold, Eli was sitting on his seat by the road watching, for his heart30 trembled for God31’s ark. When the man32 came into the city and told about it, all the city cried out.33 14 When Eli heard the noise of the crying, he said, “What does the noise of this tumult mean?” The man34 hurried, and came and told Eli.35 15 Now Eli was ninety-eight years old. His eyes were set, so that he could not see.36 16 The man37 said to Eli, “I am he who came out of the army, and I fled today out of the army.” He said, “How did the matter go, my son?”38 17 He who brought the news answered, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been also a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons also, Hophni and Phinehas, are dead, and God39’s ark has been captured.”40 18 When he made mention of God41’s ark, Eli fell from off his seat backward by the side of the gate; and his neck broke, and he died, for he was an old man42 and heavy. He had judged Israel forty years.43✦ 19 His daughter-in-law, Phinehas’ wife, was with child, near to giving birth. When she heard the news that God44’s ark was taken and that her father-in-law and her husband were dead, she bowed herself and gave birth; for her pains came on her.4546 20 About the time of her death the women who stood by her said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for you have given birth to a son.” But she didn’t answer, neither did she regard it.4748 21 She named the child Ichabod49, saying, “The glory50 has departed51 from Israel!” because God52’s ark was taken, and because of her father-in-law and her husband.53✦ 22 She said, “The glory54 has departed from Israel; for God55’s ark has been taken.”

1✦1 Now the Philistines had taken God2’s ark, and they brought it from Ebenezer to Ashdod.3✦ 2 The Philistines took God4’s ark, and brought it into the house of Dagon and set it by Dagon.56✦ 3 When the people of Ashdod arose early on the next day, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before Yahweh’s ark7. They took Dagon and set him in his place again.8910✦ 4 When they arose early on the following morning, behold, Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground11 before Yahweh’s ark; and the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands were cut off on the threshold. Only Dagon’s torso was intact.121314✦ 5 Therefore neither the priests of Dagon nor any who come into Dagon’s house step on the threshold of Dagon in Ashdod to this day. 6 But Yahweh’s hand was heavy on the people of Ashdod, and he destroyed them and struck them with tumors15, even Ashdod and its borders.161718✦ 7 When the men of Ashdod saw that it was so, they said, “The ark of the God19 of Israel shall not stay with us, for his hand is severe on us and on Dagon our god.”✦ 8 They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and said, “What shall we do with the ark of the God20 of Israel?” They answered, “Let the ark of the God of Israel be carried over to Gath.” They carried the ark of the God of Israel there.21✦ 9 It was so, that after they had carried it there, Yahweh’s hand was against the city with a very great confusion; and he struck the men of the city, both small and great, so that tumors broke out on them.2223✦ 10 So they sent God24’s ark to Ekron. As God’s ark came to Ekron, the Ekronites cried out, saying, “They have brought the ark of the God of Israel here to us, to kill us and our people.”25✦ 11 They sent therefore and gathered together all the lords of the Philistines, and they said, “Send the ark of the God26 of Israel away, and let it go again to its own place, that it not kill us and our people.” For there was a deadly panic throughout all the city. The hand of God was very heavy there.27✦ 12 The men who didn’t die were struck with the tumors; and the cry of the city went up to heaven28.

6

1✦1 Yahweh’s ark was in the country of the Philistines seven months. 23✦ 2The Philistines called for the priests and the diviners, saying, “What shall we do with Yahweh’s ark? Show us how we should send it to its place.”45✦ 3 They said, “If you send away the ark of the God6 of Israel, don’t send it empty7; but by all means return a trespass offering to him. Then you will be healed, and it will be known to you why his hand is not removed from you.”8✦ 4 Then they said, “What should the trespass offering be which we shall return to him?” They said, “Five golden tumors and five golden mice9, for the number of the lords of the Philistines; for one plague was on you all, and on your lords.1011✦ 5 Therefore you shall make images of your tumors and images of your mice that mar the land12; and you shall give glory13 to the God14 of Israel. Perhaps he will release his hand from you, from your gods, and from your land.15✦ 6 Why then do you harden your hearts as the Egyptians and Pharaoh hardened their hearts? When he had worked wonderfully among them, didn’t they let the people go, and they departed?16✦ 7 “Now therefore take and prepare yourselves a new cart and two milk cows on which there has come no yoke; and tie the cows to the cart, and bring their calves home from them;1718✦ 8 and take Yahweh’s ark and lay it on the cart. Put the jewels of gold, which you return him for a trespass offering, in a box by its side; and send it away, that it may go.192021✦ 9 Behold, if it goes up by the way of its own border to Beth Shemesh, then he has done us this great evil; but if not, then we shall know that it is not his hand that struck us. It was a chance that happened to us.”22✦ 10 The men did so, and took two milk cows and tied them to the cart, and shut up their calves at home.23✦ 11 They put Yahweh’s ark on the cart, and the box with the golden mice and the images of their tumors.2425✦ 12 The cows took the straight way by the way to Beth Shemesh. They went along the highway, lowing as they went, and didn’t turn away to the right hand or to the left; and the lords of the Philistines went after them to the border of Beth Shemesh.26✦ 13 The people of Beth Shemesh were reaping their wheat harvest in the valley; and they lifted up their eyes and saw the ark, and rejoiced to see it.27✦ 14 The cart came into the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh, and stood there, where there was a great stone. Then they split the wood of the cart and offered up the cows for a burnt offering to Yahweh.2829✦ 15 The Levites took down Yahweh’s ark and the box that was with it, in which the jewels of gold were, and put them on the great stone; and the men of Beth Shemesh offered burnt offerings and sacrificed sacrifices the same day to Yahweh.3031✦ 16 When the five lords of the Philistines had seen it, they returned to Ekron the same day.32✦ 17 These are the golden tumors which the Philistines returned for a trespass offering to Yahweh: for Ashdod one, for Gaza one, for Ashkelon one, for Gath one, for Ekron one;3334✦ 18 and the golden mice, according to the number of all the cities of the Philistines belonging to the five lords, both of fortified cities and of country villages, even to the great stone on which they set down Yahweh’s ark. That stone remains to this day in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh.3536✦ 19 He struck of the men of Beth Shemesh, because they had looked into Yahweh’s ark, he struck fifty thousand seventy37 of the men. Then the people mourned, because Yahweh had struck the people with a great slaughter.3839✦ 20 The men of Beth Shemesh said, “Who is able to stand before Yahweh, this holy40 God41? To whom shall he go up from us?”4243 21 They sent messengers to the inhabitants of Kiriath Jearim, saying, “The Philistines have brought back Yahweh’s ark. Come down and bring it up to yourselves.”

121 The men of Kiriath Jearim came and took Yahweh’s ark, and brought it into Abinadab’s house on the hill, and consecrated Eleazar his son to keep Yahweh’s ark.3456✦ 2 From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long—for it was twenty years; and all the house of Israel lamented after Yahweh.789✦ 3 Samuel spoke to all the house of Israel, saying, “If you are returning to Yahweh with all your heart, then put away the foreign gods and the Ashtaroth from among you, and direct your hearts to Yahweh, and serve him only; and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines.”10111213✦ 4 Then the children of Israel removed the Baals and the Ashtaroth, and served Yahweh only.1415 5 Samuel said, “Gather all Israel to Mizpah, and I will pray to Yahweh for you.”1617✦ 6 They gathered together to Mizpah, and drew water18, and poured it out before Yahweh, and fasted on that day, and said there, “We have sinned against Yahweh.” Samuel judged the children of Israel in Mizpah.1920✦ 7 When the Philistines heard that the children of Israel were gathered together at Mizpah, the lords of the Philistines went up against Israel. When the children of Israel heard it, they were afraid of the Philistines.2122✦ 8 The children of Israel said to Samuel, “Don’t stop crying to Yahweh our God23 for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.”2425✦ 9 Samuel took a suckling lamb, and offered it for a whole burnt offering to Yahweh. Samuel cried to Yahweh for Israel, and Yahweh answered him.2627✦ 10 As Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines came near to battle against Israel; but Yahweh thundered with a great thunder on that day on the Philistines and confused them; and they were struck down before Israel.2829✦ 11 The men of Israel went out of Mizpah and pursued the Philistines, and struck them until they came under Beth Kar.3031✦ 12 Then Samuel took a stone and set it between Mizpah and Shen, and called its name Ebenezer32, saying, “Yahweh helped us until now.”33343536✦ 13 So the Philistines were subdued, and they stopped coming within the border of Israel. Yahweh’s hand was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel37.3839✦ 14 The cities which the Philistines had taken from Israel were restored to Israel, from Ekron even to Gath; and Israel recovered its border out of the hand of the Philistines. There was peace40 between Israel and the Amorites.41✦ 15 Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.42✦ 16 He went from year to year in a circuit to Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah; and he judged Israel in all those places.43✦ 17 His return was to Ramah, for his house was there, and he judged Israel there; and he built an altar to Yahweh there.

12✦1 When Samuel was old, he made his sons judges over Israel. 3 2Now the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah. They were judges in Beersheba.45 3 His sons didn’t walk in his ways, but turned away after dishonest gain, took bribes, and perverted justice.6✦ 4 Then all the elders of Israel gathered themselves together and came to Samuel to Ramah.7 5 They said to him, “Behold, you are old, and your sons don’t walk in your ways. Now make us a king to judge us like all the nations8.”9✦ 6 But the thing displeased Samuel when they said, “Give us a king to judge us.” Samuel prayed to Yahweh.101112 7 Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to the voice of the people in all that they tell you; for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected me13 as the king over them.1415✦ 8 According to all the works which they have done since the day that I brought them up out of Egypt even to this day, in that they have forsaken me and served other gods, so they also do to you.16✦ 9 Now therefore, listen to their voice. However, you shall protest solemnly to them, and shall show them the way of the king who will reign over them.”17✦ 10 Samuel told all Yahweh’s words to the people who asked him for a king.1819✦ 11 He said, “This will be the way of the king20 who shall reign over you: he will take your sons and appoint them as his servants, for his chariots and to be his horsemen; and they will run before his chariots.21✦ 12 He will appoint them to him for captains of thousands and captains of fifties; and he will assign some to plow his ground22 and to reap his harvest; and to make his instruments of war and the instruments of his chariots.23✦ 13 He will take your daughters to be perfumers, to be cooks, and to be bakers.2425✦ 14 He will take your fields, your vineyards, and your olive groves, even your best, and give them to his servants.26✦ 15 He will take one tenth of your seed and of your vineyards, and give it to his officers and to his servants.27✦ 16 He will take your male servants, your female servants, your best young men, and your donkeys, and assign them to his own work.28✦ 17 He will take one tenth of your flocks; and you will be his servants.29✦ 18 You will cry out in that day because of your king whom you will have chosen for yourselves; and Yahweh will not answer you in that day.”3031✦ 19 But the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel; and they said, “No, but we will have a king over us,32✦ 20 that we also may be like all the nations; and that our king may judge us, and go out before us, and fight our battles.”33✦ 21 Samuel heard all the words of the people, and he rehearsed them in the ears of Yahweh.3435 22 Yahweh said to Samuel, “Listen to their voice, and make them a king.” Samuel said to the men of Israel, “Everyone go to your own city.”

123✦1 Now there was a man4 of Benjamin, whose name was Kish the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath, the son of Aphiah, the son of a Benjamite, a mighty man of valor.5✦ 2 He had a son whose name was Saul, an impressive young man6; and there was not among the children of Israel a more handsome person than he. From his shoulders and upward he was taller than any of the people.7✦ 3 The donkeys of Kish, Saul’s father, were lost. Kish said to Saul his son, “Now take one of the servants with you, and arise, go look for the donkeys.”8✦ 4 He passed through the hill country of Ephraim, and passed through the land9 of Shalishah, but they didn’t find them. Then they passed through the land of Shaalim, and they weren’t there. Then he passed through the land of the Benjamites, but they didn’t find them.1011 5 When they had come to the land12 of Zuph, Saul said to his servant who was with him, “Come! Let’s return, lest my father stop caring about the donkeys and be anxious for us.”1314 6 The servant said to him, “Behold now, there is a man15 of God16 in this city, and he is a man who is held in honor. All that he says surely happens. Now let’s go there. Perhaps he can tell us which way to go.”✦ 7 Then Saul said to his servant, “But behold, if we go, what should we bring the man17? For the bread is spent in our sacks, and there is not a present to bring to the man of God18. What do we have?”19✦ 8 The servant answered Saul again and said, “Behold, I have in my hand the fourth part of a shekel of silver. I will give that to the man20 of God21, to tell us our way.”22✦ 9 (In earlier times in Israel, when a man23 went to inquire of God24, he said, “Come! Let’s go to the seer;” for he who is now called a25 prophet was before called a seer.)26✦ 10 Then Saul said to his servant, “Well said. Come! Let’s go.” So they went to the city where the man27 of God28 was.29 11 As they went up the ascent to the city, they found young maidens going out to draw water30, and said to them, “Is the seer here?”✦ 12 They answered them and said, “He is. Behold, he is before you. Hurry now, for he has come today into the city; for the people have a sacrifice today in the high place.31✦ 13 As soon as you have come into the city, you will immediately find him before he goes up to the high place to eat; for the people will not eat until he comes, because he blesses the sacrifice. Afterwards those who are invited eat. Now therefore go up; for at this time you will find him.”32✦ 14 They went up to the city. As they came within the city, behold, Samuel came out toward them to go up to the high place.33 15 Now Yahweh had revealed to Samuel a day before Saul came, saying,3435✦ 16 “Tomorrow about this time I will send you a man36 out of the land37 of Benjamin, and you shall anoint him to be prince over my people Israel38. Go up before me to the high place, for you are to eat with me today. In the morning I will let you go and will tell you all that is in your heart43.44 20 As for your donkeys who were lost three days ago, don’t set your mind on them, for they have been found. For whom does all Israel desire? Is it not you and all your father’s house?” 21 Saul answered, “Am I not a Benjamite, of the smallest of the tribes of Israel?45 And my family the least of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin? Why then do you speak to me like this?”46 22 Samuel took Saul and his servant and brought them into the guest room, and made them sit in the best place among those who were invited, who were about thirty persons.47✦ 23 Samuel said to the cook, “Bring the portion which I gave you, of which I said to you, ‘Set it aside.’”✦ 24 The cook took up the thigh, and that which was on it, and set it before Saul. ↩ ◇ Note. Ruth as counterweight to Judges. The book opens by anchoring itself to the same era as Judges — but its register is opposite: domestic, pastoral, quiet, ending in a marriage and a baby rather than civil war and a dismembered body. In the Jewish canon Ruth is one of the Five Megillot among the Writings (read on Shavuot, the harvest festival); in the Christian canon Ruth follows Judges, completing the Judges-era picture. The Megillot placement emphasizes Ruth’s liturgical and harvest themes; the Christian placement emphasizes the chronology and the bridge to David.

Kanaf (כָּנָף) — “wing, corner of a garment.” The same word is used metaphorically here (refuge under God’s wings) and literally in 3:9 when Ruth asks Boaz to spread his kanaf over her — the marriage-protection idiom. The doubled use is intentional: Boaz invokes God’s sheltering wing in chapter 2; Ruth in chapter 3 invites Boaz to embody it. The book’s theological elegance is built on small verbal hooks like this.

↩ ◇ Note. The threshing-floor scene. The chapter is masterfully ambiguous. Naomi’s instructions (uncover his feet — possibly a euphemism — and lie down) and Ruth’s execution of them have invited centuries of debate about exactly what passes between Ruth and Boaz that night. The text is reticent on purpose: what matters is that Ruth, again, takes the initiative; Boaz, again, blesses her for hesed; and the narrative resolves toward marriage rather than scandal. The scene is one of the few in the Hebrew Bible where a woman engineers her own legal status with full agency, and the narrator reports it approvingly.

He was a kinsman of Mahlon, her first husband. (2.) The name given (for what reason is unknown) to one of the two (the other was called Jachin) brazen pillars which Solomon erected in the court of the temple (1 Kings 7:21; 2 Chronicles 3:17). These pillars were broken up and carried to Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.
